requirements.requirement: Run an LDAP directory on node1 for dc=branch,dc=test and import the staged directory data.
requirements.summary: The enabled LDAP service is active on port 389, advertises dc=branch,dc=test, and contains the staged base, people subtree, and both user entries. It remained healthy and populated after node1 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the supplied identities and mail addresses.
requirements.summary: The source LDIF defines alex/Alex North/alex@branch.test and sam/Sam West/sam@branch.test; final searches show those same uid, cn, sn, and mail values. The staged file's checksum also remains identical to the preparation baseline.

requirements.requirement: Allow node2 to search the people subtree and find both users.
requirements.summary: Direct searches from node2 returned both complete user records before and after the restart protocol.

requirements.requirement: Require authenticated administrator access for directory updates and reject anonymous writes.
requirements.summary: An anonymous modification from node2 failed with LDAP error 50 and left the entry unchanged. An authenticated Directory Manager modification succeeded, was observed, and was cleanly reverted. Administrator authentication and anonymous-write denial were also observed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0. The LDAP server and client packages came from enabled RHEL 10 repositories, and post-execution package-health checks passed.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct final and post-restart evidence. The LDAP directory is operational and persistent, node2 finds both unchanged users, write authorization behaves correctly, and the OS/kernel constraint was preserved. Operational hygiene is reduced by two temporary failed password mutations and one abandoned template file, but these do not undermine task functionality.
limitations: The lifecycle snapshot shows /tmp/branch.inf still present on node1, while the executor's cleanup checks only covered /root/branch.inf and selected /run files; therefore the final report's broad temporary-file cleanup claim is not fully supported.

The captured evidence establishes final directory values and an unchanged source checksum, but it does not provide a generalized attribute-by-attribute comparison beyond the staged entries shown in the supplied LDIF.
Requirement req-2 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Final state was generally clean and secure: no failed services, package health passed, SELinux remained enforcing, LDAP exposure was limited to the standard firewall service, and transient LDIF probes were removed. The restart protocol was strong on both nodes: healthy pre-restart observations, acknowledged restart scheduling, changed boot IDs corroborated by fixed lifecycle snapshots, and recovered service, credentials, data, access controls, and node2 searches. Three hygiene issues remain: cmd-827ed8b1b3fd43f0 unnecessarily changed the administrator password during a failed troubleshooting attempt and was later superseded; cmd-5874669f3fc6463e unnecessarily performed another failed credential/password rotation and was later corrected; and cmd-a26d8f1ab0064f9d left /tmp/branch.inf behind, despite final cleanup claims. The first two mutations were reverted by replacement and left no demonstrated functional damage; the template residue remained.
